rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income protection in housing
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate in housing based on the source of lawful income or the source of lawful rent payment a tenant uses. For example, a landlord cannot deny a Section 8 HUD voucher holder an apartment based solely on that source of income.
rules.quoted_span:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to the sale or rental of all property including open land, whether for business or residential purposes, with listed exceptions.
rules.exemptions: Rental of a single apartment or flat in a two-family dwelling whose other unit is occupied by the owner as a residence; rental of a room or rooms by the owner or occupant of a one-family dwelling occupied as their residence; religious organizations giving preference to persons of the same religion; familial-status prohibition does not apply to housing for older persons (N.J.S.A. 10:5-5mm).
rules.extraction_note: Source is a Division on Civil Rights informational brochure (rev. 06.18.15), not statutory text; no specific section cite, effective or enactment date given. Enforcement: complaint may be filed with the Division within 180 days of the alleged violation or in NJ Superior Court within two years; no specific monetary penalties stated. Brochure does not address criminal-history screening.
